target_moa.text: Atypical antipsychotic; efficacy thought to be mediated through combined central dopamine D2 and serotonin 5-HT2A receptor antagonism; lurasidone is a high-affinity antagonist at D2 (Ki=0.994 nM), 5-HT2A (Ki=0.47 nM) and 5-HT7 (Ki=0.495 nM) and a partial agonist at 5-HT1A.

citations.quote: It has been suggested that the efficacy of lurasidone in schizophrenia is mediated through a combination of central dopamine Type 2 (D2) and serotonin Type 2 (5HT2A) receptor antagonism.

In vitro receptor binding studies revealed that lurasidone is an antagonist with high affinity at dopamine D2 receptors (Ki = 0.994 nM) and the 5-hydroxytryptamine (5-HT, serotonin) receptors 5-HT2A (Ki = 0.47 nM) and 5-HT7 (Ki = 0.495 nM), is an antagonist with moderate affinity at human \alpha_2 adrenergic receptors (Ki = 10.8 nM), is a partial agonist at serotonin 5-HT1A (Ki = 6.38 nM) receptor

key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (incidence >=5% and at least twice placebo) were somnolence, akathisia, nausea, parkinsonism and agitation. Somnolence was reported in 22.3% (224/1004) of LATUDA vs 9.9% (45/455) placebo; akathisia incidence was 15.0% vs 3.3% placebo; nausea 12% vs 6% placebo. Akathisia and somnolence were dose-related.

citations.quote: **Commonly Observed Adverse Reactions:** The most common adverse reactions (incidence \ge 5\% and at least twice the rate of placebo) in patients treated with LATUDA were somnolence, akathisia, nausea, parkinsonism and agitation.
In short-term, placebo-controlled trials, somnolence was reported in 22.3% (224/1004) of patients treated with LATUDA compared to 9.9% (45/455) of placebo patients, respectively.

In the short-term, placebo-controlled schizophrenia studies, for LATUDA-treated patients, the incidence of reported EPS-related events, excluding akathisia and restlessness, was 14.7% versus 5.1% for placebo-treated patients; and the incidence of akathisia for LATUDA-treated patients was 15.0% versus 3.3% for placebo-treated patients. Akathisia appeared to be dose-related and the greatest frequency of parkinsonism and dystonia occurred with the highest dose of LATUDA, 120 mg/day (Table 8).
